quest.title: Both Brains and Brawn
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3, Pankration Fonta Cup x1, Credit Coupons x900

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You're... Genevieve, right? What brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Well I'm here to do some Pankration, but... what are YOU doing here? You aren't hoping to sign up too... are you?

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: #Ah, I know you two. Sorry, the {M#blond}{F#blonde} one can't participate.

choices.text: What!? Discrimination!?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #That was worded a little misleadingly. I think what you mean is that {NICKNAME} specifically is banned from taking part, not blonds as an entire category. Correct?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Because I'm blonde, and... you let me sign up.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Lemme put it this way: A Pankration match is a spectator sport. Entertaining the audience is more important than who wins and who loses.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: #I've heard all about your past deeds. If we let {NICKNAME} enter the ring, the outcome is a foregone conclusion, and all the anticipation is removed from the equation.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: No one wants to watch a match with a predictable outcome. If I let you take part, I might as well hand you the trophy right now and save everyone the trouble...

choices.text: Sounds like a plan. Hand it over.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not very sportsmanlike!

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: #How about... I let {NICKNAME} join as a coach? You can coach her.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: The strongest coach paired with the weakest contestant... Yeah, that should be a nice gimmick. Nice touch, I mean. For the audience.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Also — although it's mostly for fun, there's a pretty generous prize for the winner. All thanks to her colleague... Or should I say former colleague?

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: The winning team will receive Credit Coupons as well as a fantastic Fonta Trophy! Show it at the Fontaine Research Institute and you can drink all the Fonta you like, for free!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #An endless supply of free Fonta? {NICKNAME}! Paimon wants that!

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Well, if {NICKNAME} is willing to coach me and Poiret to victory, I'd be more than happy to give you the trophy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you sure? ...You're really willing to give up an endless supply of free Fonta?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Of course. I've, uh... had more than my fair share of Fonta in my time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awesome! Anyway, so you're teaming up with Poiret again, huh? ...Uh-oh, are Rave and Darcy competing this time too?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Darcy isn't, as far as I know. And Rave... I doubt he'll feel the need to. He did take all our Coupons, after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Didn't he return them to you after the results were announced!?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Nope. And I haven't seen him since. It's possible that he's left for good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: There are multiple factors that may have contributed to my previous losses. But we can't change the past, and from an efficiency perspective, competing in the Pankration tournament may prove to be the better choice now.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Especially with {NICKNAME}'s help. That would be perfect.

choices.text: For the sake of unlimited Fonta, I'll do it. I'll coach you.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #So you'll help? Fantastic! Coach {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's go find Poiret. I wonder if he has recruited any new teammates?

choices.text: Hmm... As coach, do I get any compensation besides a potential trophy?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: If the trophy isn't enough, I'm willing to compensate you for your trouble. I'll do my best to make it worth your time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Sounds like a sweet deal. Let's help them, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: How about I use only one hand to fight?

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Oh? Hmm, that might spice things up a little, but... Nope, I don't think that'll work. What if you actually win the tournament with one hand? It would set the bar too high for future tournaments.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: I know I said entertainment value is key, but we also have to be careful to manage the audience's expectations.

choices.text: In that case, Paimon can fight on my behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No way! Paimon fights as a duo with {NICKNAME}, or not at all!

choices.text: I never said I wanted to take part.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has... Wait, what's the opposite of deja vu? Anyway, Paimon has that. Because the last time we were in a situation like this, both Darcy and Estienne were practically begging us to participate...

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: How's it going, Poiret? Will he be joining our team?

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Hah. Hard pass.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I believe that's a "no."

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: As much as I enjoy the detective jokes, from what I've seen of your combat capabilities, you're about as good in a fight as a Blubberbeast.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Joining your team would be like debuting on stage just before the curtains close.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: If I had time for that, don't you think I'd be better off rehearsing for the Tri-Coupon Troupe's performance?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: You make a lot of good points. But I would like to refute one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I may have lost to Roussimoff in unarmed combat, but I've changed my fighting style since then. Now, I can at least draw in a fight with a Sternshield Crab.

choices.text: A Sternshield Crab is competing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon highly doubts that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What a pity. Such a delicious opponent...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Might I add that {NICKNAME} has agreed to coach us. I'm sure we stand a much greater chance of winning with help from {M#him}{F#her}.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: The best coach can't help a lost cause... But you said you'd changed your fighting style?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Yes. Close-quarter combat is not my forte, so I've prepared numerous bottles... filled with Cryo energy.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: With these, I can slow down my opponents in the arena. And also treat them to a delicious ice-cold Fonta outside the ring, to maintain cordial relations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's so jealous... Wait, is that how bottles of Cryo are supposed to be used?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I'll stick with my axe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What? Aren't you a researcher? Where'd you learn to use an axe?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Rest assured that I'm quite handy with an axe. I chop firewood for stress-relief when my research hits a wall.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So many questions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Eh, Paimon won't ask.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: #I have a suggestion. Why don't we have a little sparring session now? That way, you can show me your skills, and Coach {NICKNAME} can get a sense of your fighting styles. What do you think?

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Depending on how the sparring goes... I may or may not decide to join your team.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Hmm... Seems like a reasonable suggestion. What do you think, Poiret?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Yes, excellent suggestion. If only you'd come up with it sooner... I think I've used up all my mental energy on making detective jokes.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Hahaha. Well, I would say let's get right to the Pankration Ring and not waste any more time, but... Are you sure you're dressed for a sparring match?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: What do you mean? I always dress like this when I'm chopping firewood...

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: You should change into something that's easier to move around in. Fortunately, the troupe has some costumes — give me a minute...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Goncourt gets a set of comfortable clothes for Genevieve.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's your opponent though. Isn't it counter-productive to help her...?

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: It's not a fair fight if she's handicapped by her clothes.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Thank you, you're very considerate. Whichever way this goes, you have my respect as an opponent.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Haha. Alright, I can officially say it now: Let's get right to the Pankration Ring and not waste any more time! I'm sure Roussimoff won't mind us borrowing it for a while.

choices.text: Unarmed combat? With Roussimoff? You?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Yes. I realize now that it was a reckless decision on my part, so I've decided to avoid unarmed combat from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: We'd like to use this place to train with Goncourt.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Sure thing. No problem at all.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: #Please observe our fight closely, Coaches {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Truth be told, Poiret and I lack fighting experience... especially this kind of fighting, so...

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>Please let us know right away if you have any advice during the fight.</color>

choices.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Now, let's warm up and get ready to enter the arena.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Goncourt can't be stronger than a Sternshield Crab, right? You can do it!

choices.text: What if I give bad advice...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I trust your judgment. As long as it isn't a fatal mistake, there's always a chance to turn it around, right?

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Not bad. I'm impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: It was close. Could have gone either way!

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Ah, I've been waiting sooo long for a chance to say that.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Erm... but it was two against one, so based on Goncourt's pankration ethics, this probably didn't count as a fair fight.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: No, no, it absolutely counts. The rules allow it. Plus, I was going easy on you — you're new to this, after all.

choices.text: That was you going easy? ...Really?

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: What would be the point? I was only testing their skills, why would I want to risk injuring them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fair point... Well anyway, since they impressed you, are you willing to join our team now?

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Haha. Hard pass.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the...!?

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: #I may have chosen to join if it was just the two of them. But with {NICKNAME} here, I'm somewhat superfluous.

choices.text: Am I really that awesome? I had no idea.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Oh please, you're not kidding anyone. Excessive humility is no different from arrogance.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: #Anyway, I'm sure you'll put on an amazing performance with {NICKNAME} coaching. As for me... I'll be cheering you on from the audience.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Oh, and although I won't be fighting alongside you, I'd be happy to provide some support outside of the ring.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Considering that your fighting styles are a little monotonous... Let's go get you kitted out with some more stuff. And the coach, of course — there's a few things that might come in handy.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Our troupe is really well equipped... It makes me wonder, how come our performances are always sub-par?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope these things are as good as you're claiming.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Oh, don't you worry. They are. Anyway, seeing is believing — let's go to Alvard. He keeps hold of all the stuff I order for the troupe.

choices.text: Thanks for the compliment.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: I'm only speaking the truth.

choices.text: Why didn't you go all out?

talks.objective: Go to the Rag and Bone Shop

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: The props should be around here... They'll be packed in some flimsy wooden boxes.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: If you find them, go ahead and <color=#00E1FFFF>crack them open</color>.

talks.objective: Break the wooden boxes and recover the props

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck is all this!? Does your troupe really use these in your performances?

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Using them is optional, but having them is mandatory. That's my motto!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I know nothing about performing... So I'll take your word for it, Goncourt.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: ...Wait, but this is a fight, not a performance... right?

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Yes, but it's still for entertainment purposes. The Pankration Ring can be considered a stage of sorts. I look forward to watching you shine on the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: With all your preparation so far, I'm sure your first fight will be a breeze. I heard your opponent is a big blue fella, and while he might be a stocky guy, I don't think he's a match for you.

choices.text: Goncourt seems like a better coach than me...

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: #You're too kind. My assistance has been minimal. I'll leave the hard work to you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Coach {NICKNAME}, could you ask Roussimoff when the matches will officially begin? We'll be ready to fight whenever you say the word.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: I'll watch your fights if I have the time. Best of luck in the tournament!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks for everything! You're a great guy.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Haha, and thanks to Poiret for the detective jokes. I'm hoping to work some of them into my scripts. If any of you have any good ideas for a story, do let me know.

choices.text: Sure. I've got plenty of stories to share.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: Perfect! We'll have to talk more sometime.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: One thing at a time, Coach. C'mon, let's go see Roussimoff.

choices.text: As long as I get credited. And a copyright fee.

response.speaker: Goncourt
response.text: I'm sure we can arrange that!

choices.text: Do you need my help with anything?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Our first opponent won't be that difficult, right? So let's use the same system as we did before — just give us any input you think we need during the fight.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Back so soon?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Fast and furious.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Yeah... fast to lose, furious in defeat...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you being so pessimistic!?

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Sounds like holding all those Cryo bottles has cooled his enthusiasm, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Huh? So, elemental energy really does have that kind of effect? Of course! The Fontaine Research Institute was right after all. Instead of elemental energy—

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: ...If you're ready, you can start whenever you like.

choices.text: Aren't you going to explain the joke?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: What joke?

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Nothing! Just forget I said anything...

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Ahem, now then — your first opponent has quite an interesting origin story. He was stuffed into a barrel, and the barrel had a note on it that said: Take a look in the mirror.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Obviously, the person who stuffed him in the barrel is also participating. So if he beats you, it'll be his chance at revenge in the ring.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: After all, fighting's prohibited outside the ring — it's his only chance to win a fight and not get punished for it. Of course, he'll still be entitled to visit the infirmary if he loses.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: So. Are you ready to enter the ring?

choices.text: We're ready.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Then please take your positions.

choices.text: I need a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing.

choices.text: I'm good to go.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Congratulations to the researcher and research assistant! A first-bout victory for our first-time fighters!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: As for the guy in the barrel, don't be discouraged! We'll see you again in the next competition!

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Ugh, that Roussimoff... I am NOT a research assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Hey, a research assistant is a very good job. Maybe you should consider it. If nothing else, working at the Fontaine Research Institute would be much better job security than working as a detective's assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Fair enough, I'll give it some thought. If I ever manage to leave this place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So how did the two of you team up, anyway? You seem like very different personalities, and you don't have much common ground professionally, either.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: That's not entirely true. The truth is, I was doing an investigation at the Fontaine Research Institute before I came here. Everything was going fine until I ran into that Melusine...

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I was just gathering evidence, but she insisted that it was theft.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Define "gathering evidence"...

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Taking private documents from the Fontaine Research Institute, which would generally be considered as constituting theft.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I'll have you know they were problematic documents. Anyway, I pleaded guilty and accepted my punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like there's an interesting story here...

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I'm not at liberty to divulge the details of the case, as it would violate client confidentiality.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I'm all too familiar with the subject of his investigation. I injured them during a conference...

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Ma'am, please! Stop! What did I JUST say about divulging details!?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Oh! Sorry. Yeah, it's nothing to do with the competition, anyway, so we shouldn't bore our poor coach with all this.

choices.text: I'd be happy to keep listening for a little extra compensation.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: You want us to violate my client's terms of engagement, and my code of professional ethics, AND pay you for the privilege!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She} was just joking! ...Right?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Alright, let's get back to business. Coach, in your professional opinion, what do we need to improve on?

choices.text: Strength.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Paimon thinks Genevieve has them both covered for strength, swinging that axe around...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Strength, huh... Definitely an important factor, but not something we can really improve on in a short timeframe...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Even Pure Water has its limits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Perhaps focusing on technique would be better for fast results?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, both Genevieve and Poiret rely on throwing. Faster and more accurate throws would give them an advantage, whether it's a bottle of Cryo or some stage firecrackers, right?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Sounds good. Shall we find somewhere to practice our throwing techniques?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: As long as we can find a spot where we won't disturb anyone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a big empty space near the Rift of Erosion... I think that should work? Let's head over and check it out!

choices.text: Accuracy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, accuracy's important. Every missed shot is just more energy wasted.

choices.text: Speed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Speed helps you dodge enemy attacks and land more strikes in the same amount of time!

choices.text: I'm very curious about what goes on at the Fontaine Research Institute behind closed doors...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Heh, you can probably read all about it in The Steambird or some detective novel... Though I can't vouch for the credibility in either case.

talks.objective: Go to the Rift of Erosion

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This looks like a great place to practice throwing!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Goncourt gave us a bunch of stuff earlier. Some of it should come in handy here...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Genevieve and Poiret set up a practice area...

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: It's a little jerry-rigged... but it should be fit for purpose. Coach, why don't you give us a demonstration first?

choices.text: My pleasure.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: We're counting on you, Coach.

choices.text: Watch and learn.

talks.objective: Demonstrate throwing techniques to the pair

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it? Any questions?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: I understand it in principle, but...

choices.text: Shall I demonstrate again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, maybe we should let them have some practice now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you need hand-eye coordination. Speaking of which, Poiret has to wear glasses. Will your poor eyesight affect your accuracy?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Oh, these are just a fashion statement. They're not prescription lenses.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? ...That must be a nuisance, surely? Wearing those in the ring?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: You just have to treat them as an extension of your body. Besides, if I take them off, no one'll recognize me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be silly!

choices.text: Don't be silly!

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Let's not get hung up on spectacles here... Is this basic training really all we can do? It reminds me of being a detective's assistant: revisiting the same crime scene over and over countless times, hoping to find a new shred of evidence...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: There's no substitute for hard work, in any field. Our coach has personally shown us how it's done. You shouldn't dismiss the value of practice before you've even tried it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! If you don't put in the time, you'll regret it down the line!

choices.text: Are we here to grumble or here to win? Put your back into it!

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Yes, Coach! Of course, Coach!

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: It needs to be second nature when we're in the ring. Let's take turns practicing: While one of us throws, the other will watch and check their accuracy.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Alright, let's do that.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Great. Coach {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's meet again at the arena when the next round begins.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! No slacking off, Poiret!

choices.text: How about a sparring match with me instead? Be warned, I don't pull my punches.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I'll go practice throwing right away!

choices.text: Actually, everyone does look alike...
Principles won't help you. You need to practice it for yourself.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Yep. Muscle memory is the key here.

talks.objective: Go to Pankration Ring the next day between 18:00 and 22:00

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I wonder who our next opponent will be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Where's Genevieve?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: She's gone to get changed. She'll be back before the match starts.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Your opponent is ready. Let me know when you want to start.

choices.text: As soon as Genevieve gets back.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Best of luck out there!

choices.text: Still getting ready. Please give me a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: How is this possible? A samurai from afar losing to a feeble researcher and her assistant!?

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Will the newcomers' luck ever run out? Find out in the next match!
I'm warning you! It's a serious crime to fight outside the ring!

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Do you think I care at this point?
You psycho! Do you solve all your problems with brute force? No wonder you had to fake the data when you couldn't get the results you wanted...

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I'm the one who should be warning you. Unless you have evidence to back up your claims, that was blatant slander!
Oh, you didn't like that, huh? Hmph, tough cookies!
You should start thinking about how you're gonna apologize to Mr. Bossuet when you get out of here — IF you ever get out of here.
Hah, what am I saying? I should be thanking you. Mr. Bossuet had to step down thanks to your academic dishonesty.
No way can Raimondo handle all of the Fontaine Research Institute's projects on his own. Once I get out of here...

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: It never ceases to amaze me how some people can fantasize about such a bright future in this fortress where the sun never shines. A true testament to the power of the human imagination.
Who are you? And how exactly is this any of your business?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Who, me? As you can probably guess, I'm just a lowly assistant. A nobody, really.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: We're all contestants here, so let's try and be a little cordial to one other outside the ring, shall we? I have a delicious iced health drink here, very sweet. Would you care for a glass?
What? Wait, no... I'm not even a contestant.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Tsk. He didn't fall for it.
Unlike some people, I refuse to stoop to using brute force to prove my own value. A Fontaine Research Institute lab is too good for you. A lumberjack's cabin in the mountains is where you belong...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Genevieve punches him.
How dare you! Private brawls are... You all saw that too, right!? Private brawls are prohibited!

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Oh, goodness. I'm so sorry — I took my glasses off for a second, and my eyesight is terrible without them. I'm afraid I didn't see a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leave us outta this!

choices.text: I just got here. Did something happen?

response.text: Oh, great... Is anybody here not a pathological liar? No? Just my luck.
You self-righteous, conniving... Ugh, I'll wipe those smug looks off each of your faces, just you wait! My Vieille-Model Enhanced Meka will prove everything...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The man leaves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What was all that about?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I'm sorry you had to see that. I... have a bit of a short fuse. I always try my best to stay rational, objective, and neutral in all scenarios but... sometimes, I fail to control myself.

choices.text: A short fuse is no excuse for assault.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You just suddenly punched him, without saying a single word! Paimon was shocked!

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: You're right... I'm sorry. I'll try to do better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, who was he?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Champvallon. He's a senior researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute. He's always had a rivalry with Raimondo, but I guess he thinks he might be in with a chance since Bossuet has fallen from power.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: But it doesn't look like Raimondo has any intention of giving him the chance. It's a shame, really — if he was Raimondo's equal, The Steambird would have to give me my own column space.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why? Also, how do you know about all this? It's kinda suspicious...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Because when I was caught at— Ahem, when I was collecting evidence at the Fontaine Research Institute, he was the main target of my investigation. All those problematic documents I mentioned were linked to him.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I've actually met him a few times before. But he didn't seem to recognize me at all just now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec! Now you're divulging the details of the case! What happened to client confidentiality? And professional ethics?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: The fact that he's here in the Fortress of Meropide means the case is clearly over. Plus, I sent my uncle a letter recently to see if I could find anything out, and all he sent in reply was "be patient"...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I knew something weird was going on! I guess he couldn't be bothered to help me since he knew what was about to happen. Hmph, and to think I spent years running errands for him. And even let him put me as a supporting character in his novel...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I'm not surprised to see him here at all. He's never had a very good reputation at the Fontaine Research Institute. Lots of negative rumors flying around about him. Guess they weren't all groundless.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Oh... I know I was sent here for injuring him at a conference, and of course for other reasons, too... But I swear the part about his bad reputation is public knowledge.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: If you don't believe me, ask anyone else from the Fontaine Research Institute...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That won't be necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Anyway, Paimon's more concerned about that stuff he said before leaving. Isn't he not participating in the competition?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And even if he was, it's all about entertainment value, right? So why did it sound like he's plotting something nefarious?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Knowing how he operates, I'd guess he intends to take this opportunity to show what he's capable of and impress the powerful people in the Fortress.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Well, having met some engineers from the Fontaine Research Institute before, like Clynes, Paimon's gotta ask... What makes this Champvallon guy so special?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Professionally, he doesn't have any noteworthy accomplishments. But he's quite skilled at networking and playing people to his advantage. Although... Surely he wouldn't...?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: What's the worst he can throw at us? Twelve engineers, all built like two Roussimoffs?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: No, you moron, it's worse than that. Didn't you hear what he said? The "Vieille-Model Enhanced Meka."

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: It sounds like he's gonna send clockwork meka into the ring to fight us on his behalf. And not your typical Gardemeks mass-produced in the fortress, either. Some modified variety with enhanced combat capabilities.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's crazy! Clockwork meka aren't even human. How are they allowed in a pankration tournament?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Since it's just for entertainment, there are no rules stating that participants have to be human. As a matter of fact, someone once captured a Sternshield Crab from the abandoned production zone and sent that in as their fighter...

choices.text: Oh. So you really did draw in that fight, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds pretty far-fetched... But on the offchance he really does send meka into the ring, what are you gonna do?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Surrender. I know I'd be letting down our coach, but there's no way I could win that fight with this amount of training. I know my limits.

choices.text: Don't give up! Anything I can do, you can too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, get real! A few encouraging words aren't gonna magically close the gap between you and them...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: ...I think we just might have a shot, you know. If we can utilize the mutually destructive effects of pneuma and ousia energy to weaken the clockwork meka... Winning wouldn't be beyond the realms of possibility.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I have an idea, but this isn't the place to discuss it... Let's find somewhere in the production zone that's better lit.

choices.text: There's no shame in surrendering.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess there's no other choice. Poiret's just a feeble assistant, after all...

choices.text: That's absurd.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: All about that entertainment value.

choices.text: Talk smack, get whacked. He had it coming.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, he clearly knew which buttons to press... Still, you shouldn't let people provoke you. Violence is rarely the answer.

choices.text: It's not a brawl unless you hit her back.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Are you gonna fight back? No one's stopping you. But I hear it's a serious crime to fight outside the ring.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, Genevieve! So, what's your idea?

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: So as I was saying, we need to utilize the mutually destructive effects of pneuma and ousia energy to weaken the clockwork meka and create opportunities to attack.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: This is far beyond the scope of my abilities. I bid you all adieu.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Don't go! I can't accomplish this without you.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: With some processing, pneumousia can be stored in a container — even in your sugar glass bottles.

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I'm familiar with the structural weaknesses of clockwork meka. So if you create an opening, I can go in and attack.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh... That might actually work! And Poiret has been practicing his throwing, so hopefully his speed and accuracy should have improved by now.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: But I don't know anything about the principle of mutual annihilation between pneuma and ousia...

choices.text: Honestly, me neither.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: This isn't a research project, so you don't need to grapple with the theory. All you need to know is which action causes what reaction.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: First things first, help me set up a practice arena.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Genevieve and Poiret set up a practice arena...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Are these from the stage props Goncourt gave us, too?

choices.text: What kind of show would need props like these?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ummm... Maybe an educational play about the Fontaine Research Institute? To teach people about Pneumousia? ...Or something?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #The arena is ready. Now for a demonstration on the pneumousia mutual annihilation phenomenon... Over to you, Coach {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: You only need to run through it once. After that, I'll supervise Poiret's training until he knows exactly what he's doing.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Is it that necessary? How hard can it be?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Hmm... That depends on how quickly you pick it up.

choices.text: Why does he buy all this stuff?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What was it he said... Optional to use, mandatory to have, right? Paimon sure would love to have a snoop around the Tri-Coupon Troupe's warehouse. Assuming they have one.

choices.text: If you put your mind to it, I'm sure you will get it.

talks.objective: Demonstrate the destructive power of Pneumousia annihilation reactions to Poiret

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Uh... So did I help?

choices.text: Thanks, Poiret.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Is that a genuine thanks? Or a "Gee, thanks"...?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Anyway — let's meet at the pankration ring before the next match, like last time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... Don't die on us, Poiret! You need to live on!

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Oh, don't be so dramatic! The stage props are getting to your head... But sure, I'll try to avoid getting annihilated along with the pneuma and ousia.

choices.text: You'd have been a much bigger help if you did nothing.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I knew it...

talks.objective: Go to Pankration Ring the next day between 18:00 and 22:00

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: I know we can win this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Poiret. How did the training go? Did it work?

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Yep. I'm now fully versed in the mutually destructive properties of pneuma and ousia energy.

choices.text: Great. Then why don't you summarize it for me?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Sorry, I was just joking. I still don't really get how it works... But I do know what I have to do.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Good! Because you'll be facing a heavyweight this time, haha!

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Well? Ready to enter the arena?

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: #I'm ready. Don't forget to give us your input during match, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Then let's begin.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Contestants and coaches, please take your positions!

choices.text: Still getting ready. Please give me a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing!

choices.text: Congratulations. Maybe a job as a research assistant really is in the cards for you.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: #What an exhilarating match! Congratulations to the researcher and her assistant! And of course to their coach, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: But I have some breaking news! Don't get too comfortable, because this match... is entering overtime!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Your spectacular performance really put me in the mood for a brawl. So allow me to be your opponent during the overtime match!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: I accept my defeat. Looks really can be deceiving! Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: You... never said anything... about an... overtime match... I'm about to... pass out...

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: No entertainment-driven tournament would be complete without a few exciting plot twists!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Same applies to using firecrackers in the ring! Or sweet-scented sugar glass bottles!

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Without further ado, are you ready to receive your prize?

choices.text: Feels like we're forgetting something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are we? Hmm... Meh, if we forgot about it, it can't be that important!

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: ...Where did Champvallon go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Good point!

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Those meka were his pride and joy, and we tore them to shreds. Would you stick around to be humiliated further? He's probably hiding away to escape the shame.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Hmm, I doubt it... Like you said, they were his pride and joy. I don't think he's going to take this lying down...

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Ah, you've got nothing to worry about! You're the champions, and you even defeated me! You can handle whatever else he might throw at you.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Be that as it may... Fighting two matches back to back has completely exhausted me. I need to sit down, or I'm gonna faint...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: Right now, he could throw a newborn puppy at me and I'd probably lose the fight...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Champvallon returns, and he's brought some "friends"...

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: My Vieille-Model Enhanced Meka... You destroyed my Vieille-Model Enhanced Meka!

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: This tournament isn't over yet!

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Ugh... Leave him to me. I've still got some fight in me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! Don't force yourself!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I guess it's my time to shine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah! Let Coach {NICKNAME} show you how it's done!

choices.text: The Fonta Trophy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Unlimited Fonta!

dialogues.speaker: Champvallon
dialogues.text: Enough! No more! Please, stop!

choices.text: Already? I'm still warming up here.

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: You... all that Mora... all those Coupons!

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: You're completely mad, all of you... No more messing with crazy. I'm done!

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: Ugh, I should have known after last time... What a spectacular failure this was. I'm admitting defeat, and I'm leaving.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Not without me, you're not! Let's find somewhere to discuss reimbursement for my losses. Just look at the mess you've made of my precious Pankration Ring...

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Oh, but first — it gives me great pleasure to present the champions with the grand prize! Be proud of yourselves. You've earned it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Roussimoff and Champvallon leave...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was pretty underwhelming in the end. Feels like all that preparation was a lot of effort for nothing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But it was worth it to see {NICKNAME} in the ring! So cool! Hehe!

choices.text: Yeah. I hope you were taking notes.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I think this learning opportunity is a little wasted on me...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #We promised the trophy to Coach {NICKNAME} and Paimon. As for the Credit Coupons...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I feel bad — you went above and beyond by taking that last fight, so we should really increase your compensation... But we really need those Coupons. We can give you a little extra, but not as much as you deserve...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ah yes. You're running low on coupons after Rave, uh... Anyway, it's fine. We'll stick to the amount originally agreed. Right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: That's alright with me.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: #Thank you so much, Coach {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So. What are your plans now that you've won the tournament and gotten a big stash of Coupons?

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: All I can think about is life after the Fortress of Meropide...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Although it's true that they have no evidence to prove I committed academic dishonesty, the fact is I also haven't been able to reproduce the results from the disputed experiment...

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: I'll just have to keep going with my research and find a way to prove myself.

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: This place isn't that bad, but the world beyond the fortress suits me better. Clients are hard to come by down here. There's practically zero work for a detective...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: But then again, even in the rest of Fontaine, the detective industry is just too competitive... Hmm. Maybe I should think about expanding outside of Fontaine...

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: #Coach {NICKNAME}, you're a traveler, right? Maybe we'll run into each other somewhere else one day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like you have great plans. Paimon hopes you achieve all your goals!

response.speaker: Poiret
response.text: I hope I'll have at least graduated from being a supporting character in my uncle's novels when we next meet, haha.

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: Thank you, and good luck to you too!

choices.text: I'm not in this to bleed anyone dry...
Ah, I don't know about "cool."

response.speaker: Genevieve
response.text: You're too modest, Coach.

choices.text: Half-time break? Sure.

response.speaker: Champvallon
response.text: You want a second half!?

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Are you ready to watch the match?

choices.text: Ready.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Then let's begin.

choices.text: Give me a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: You want to use the pankration ring? Go ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Is there enough sugar? What a waste...

dialogues.speaker: Goncourt
dialogues.text: Since we're at the pankration ring, I'll go by "Goncourt IV." You can call me "The Fourth."

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: My axe... I'd better use it carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Come on, Coach. My hands are getting sweaty from the nerves. Less procrastination, more pankration...

dialogues.speaker: Genevieve
dialogues.text: Stuffed inside a barrel? How is that possible? I wonder how they did it...

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Are you ready to watch the match?

choices.text: Ready.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Then let's begin.

choices.text: Give me a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: My muscles are aching...

dialogues.speaker: Roussimoff
dialogues.text: Are you ready to watch the match?

choices.text: Ready.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Then let's begin.

choices.text: Give me a moment.

response.speaker: Roussimoff
response.text: Sure thing.

dialogues.speaker: Poiret
dialogues.text: Don't think about what's in the bottle... Just aim and throw, aim and throw...

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: Pankration Recreational Tournament now underway. Spectators welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: Latest Pankration Results: The guy in the barrel was defeated! The researcher and her assistant advance to the next round!

dialogues.speaker: Comment
dialogues.text: Detective's assistant. Not researcher's assistant.

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Comment
dialogues.text: We mustn't overlook the coach's contribution in this match. I suggest crediting them in the results.

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: #Latest Pankration Results: The samurai from afar lost in a two-against-one battle! The feeble researcher and her assistant stole the limelight thanks to their {M#blond}{F#blonde} coach's training!

dialogues.speaker: Comment
dialogues.text: Fine... Researcher's assistant it is.

dialogues.speaker: Another Person's Comment
dialogues.text: Maybe we should consider giving him a consolation prize since he came such a long way?

dialogues.speaker: And Another Person's Comment
dialogues.text: I would personally present him with an award if he helps promote Fonta in Inazuma.
